1	# Lab results with real phones, 2026-10-16
2	
3	Phones: VVX 250 (firmware 6.4.6), Edge E220 (8.2.3), and a VVX 301 (5.9.x) for the TLS check only. No CCX was
4	available. Uploaded bodies were deleted after the session because they held real call history. Each row names the
5	decision it settled.
6	
7	| Check | Result | What it changed |
8	|---|---|---|
9	| Content-Length | Always sent, never chunked. `Expect: 100-continue` on every PUT. No Content-Range. | Keep the 411 rule; the service and the ALB must handle 100-continue (ADR 0009). |
10	| MAC in the certificate | Subject CN, 12 hex digits, uppercase, no separators. No SAN. File names carry the MAC in lowercase. | Read the MAC from the CN and compare case-insensitively (ADR 0004). |
11	| TLS | TLS 1.2 only on all three phones. Shared ciphers: ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256 and ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384. | The ALB policy must allow these on TLS 1.2 (ADR 0003). |
12	| Certificate chain | Phones send 3 certificates (leaf and 2 intermediates); with the root the chain is 4. Device certificates are valid for 15 years. | Exactly at the ALB depth limit of 4, so it must be tested on a real ALB. Phones made before about late 2011 may carry expired certificates; how the ALB treats them is open. |
13	| Reaction to status codes | Retry only on 503: 3 tries, 1 s apart, identical body. Retry-After ignored. 405, 429, 413, 411, 400 and 403 get one try. A 503 sent after 100 Continue leaves app.log stuck for 300 s and holds back the phone's other uploads. | Always reject before 100 Continue. Never 503; prefer 429 when overloaded (ADR 0009). Keys must cope with identical calls.xml copies within 2 s (ADR 0011). |
14	| File names | `<mac>-app.log`, `<mac>-boot.log` (VVX only), `<mac>-calls.xml`. Manual upload: `<mac>-now-app.log`, `<mac>-now-boot.log`; `-now-` comes right after the MAC. | Accept `-now-` after the MAC. Don't require boot.log; the Edge never sends it (ADR 0007). |
15	| What each upload holds | app.log holds only the lines added since the last successful upload, plus any failed lines. `-now-` files and calls.xml are full copies every time. | Store the pieces; joining them in order rebuilds the log. Expect one full app.log per phone at migration. Nothing is lost on a 429. |
16	| Backlog after an outage | After a 15-minute outage the phone sends nothing until something new happens. No log lines or call-list changes were lost. A 1-5-9 call made during the outage was dropped. | No upload flood when the service comes back. |
17	| Other models | The Edge E220 behaves like the VVX 250 except it never sends boot.log and offers only 6 GCM ciphers. The VVX 301 matches the VVX 250 on TLS. | One design fits all three. |
18	| Sizes | app.log 283 B to 28.6 KB; calls.xml 18.5 to 64.8 KB. Every upload took under 35 ms on the LAN. No core dumps seen. | Small bodies. Core-dump sizes come from production data only (`2026-10-15-oci-measurements.md`). |
19	
20	Still open from the lab: whether the ALB accepts the phone's chain at depth 4, whether it overwrites client-sent
21	`X-Amzn-Mtls-*` headers (ADR 0004 is safe either way), and how it treats expired device certificates. These need a
22	real ALB, not the Envoy stand-in in `local/`.

1	# local/CLAUDE.md
2	
3	Rules for agents working in `local`. The root CLAUDE.md still applies.
4	
5	## What this folder is
6	
7	The local run environment: one LocalStack container (S3, SQS, DynamoDB), both services with the `local-test` profile and Envoy as the ALB stand-in for a real phone, started by `docker compose`, plus an init script that creates what the services expect. Local runs only, never deployed.
8	
9	## Commands
10	
11	From the repo root:
12	
13	- Build the jars first, because the images copy them from `target/`: `mvn clean verify` (or `mvn package -DskipTests`). Old jars there give old behavior with no warning.
14	- Once, before the first start: `local/envoy/gen-certs.sh` writes the lab CA and Envoy's server certificate for this Mac's LAN IP to `local/envoy/certs/`. It takes the IP of en0; pass another as its argument. When the IP changes, run it again (it keeps the CA), then `docker compose -f local/docker-compose.yml restart envoy`. Envoy reads `envoy.yaml`, `master.cfg` and the certificates only at start, so it needs the same restart after any change to them.
15	- Start everything: `docker compose -f local/docker-compose.yml up -d --build`. The first build pulls the 8x8 base image and needs the VPN; later runs don't. The services start once LocalStack's healthcheck sees `init-aws.sh` finish.
16	- Check it: `curl -s localhost:1297/actuator/health` (upload-service) and `curl -s localhost:1299/actuator/health` (processor), both `{"status":"UP",...}`
17	- Check the whole path: `local/smoke-test.sh` uploads one file under a random MAC, shows the S3 object and the processor's row, and exits non-zero if a check fails
18	- After changing Java code: rebuild the jars, then `up -d --build` again
19	- Empty the bucket, the table and both queues (needs `aws` and `jq` on the host): `local/reset.sh`
20	- Stop and delete everything, data included: `docker compose -f local/docker-compose.yml down`
21	- Check that Envoy turns away anything but a Poly phone in the TLS handshake, with no HTTP response and no upload-service log line:
22	
23	  ```
24	  IP=$(ipconfig getifaddr en0)
25	  curl -v --cacert local/envoy/certs/lab-ca.crt -X PUT --data-binary hello https://$IP:8443/logs/48256738509b-app.log  # alert certificate required, reason(1116) in macOS curl
26	  openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -days 1 -subj /CN=48256738509B -keyout /tmp/k.pem -out /tmp/c.pem
27	  curl -v --cacert local/envoy/certs/lab-ca.crt --cert /tmp/c.pem --key /tmp/k.pem -X PUT --data-binary hello https://$IP:8443/logs/48256738509b-app.log  # alert unknown ca
28	  ```
29	
30	- Give a phone the lab CA, once, from your own terminal. The folder holds the certificate only, never the keys: `d=$(mktemp -d) && cp local/envoy/certs/lab-ca.crt "$d" && python3 -m http.server 8080 -d "$d"`. The phone installs `http://<lan-ip>:8080/lab-ca.crt` in Platform CA 2. Stop the server afterwards.
31	- Watch the phone's requests: `docker compose -f local/docker-compose.yml logs -f envoy`, one line per request. A rejected handshake writes nothing.
32	
33	A phone reaches the stack only through Envoy on `https://<lan-ip>:8443`, with the VPN off, because the VPN routes all of 10.0.0.0/8. A request to 1296 skips Envoy and needs the `X-Amzn-Mtls-*` and `X-Forwarded-For` headers set by hand, with a leaf certificate whose CN is the MAC in uppercase, as `smoke-test.sh` does.
34	
35	## File map
36	
37	- `docker-compose.yml`: the pinned LocalStack container on port 4566, upload-service on 1296/1297 and processor on 1298/1299, built from each module's `src/main/docker/Dockerfile`, and the pinned Envoy image on 8443.
38	- `envoy/envoy.yaml`: the mTLS listener, the ALB headers and the routes. `/logs/` goes to upload-service, a GET of `<mac>.cfg` or `000000000000.cfg` gets `envoy/master.cfg`, everything else 404.
39	- `envoy/poly-ca-bundle.pem`: the three Poly CAs Envoy trusts. Public, so committed.
40	- `envoy/master.cfg`: the master config every phone gets. Logs and call lists go to `/logs/`.
41	- `envoy/gen-certs.sh`: runs on the host and writes `envoy/certs/`, which git ignores.
42	- `init/init-aws.sh`: runs inside the container when LocalStack is ready. Creates the bucket, the queue and its DLQ, the `raw/` notification and the table. Safe to run again.
43	- `reset.sh`: runs on the host against `localhost:4566`.
44	- `smoke-test.sh`: runs on the host against LocalStack and both services, not through Envoy. Sends the ALB headers itself, because only a phone has a certificate Envoy accepts.
45	
46	## Hard rules
47	
48	- Never use the `latest` LocalStack tag. Since 23 March 2026 it needs an auth token. Before changing the pinned version, check that a second `put-object` with `--if-none-match '*'` on the same key fails with `PreconditionFailed` (ADR 0011).
49	- The names are `device-logs-local` (bucket), `device-logs-uploads` and `device-logs-uploads-dlq` (queues), `device-logs-index` (table) and `us-west-2`. When one changes, change `init-aws.sh`, `reset.sh` and the `local-test` file of every service together.
50	- Redrive after 5 receives and a 60 s visibility timeout are queue settings in `init-aws.sh`, never Java constants (ADR 0023).
51	- S3 notifies the queue directly, on `raw/` only, with no EventBridge (ADR 0017).
52	- The table's sort key is named `received_at_type` and its value is `<received_at>#<type>`. The `#` stays in the value only: a `#` in an attribute name would force `ExpressionAttributeNames` on every key condition and projection. The GSI is `customer-index` on `customer_id` + `received_at` (ADR 0022).
53	- LocalStack does not enforce IAM, so a local pass does not prove the real queue policy or roles are right.
54	- Scripts here use the fixed endpoint `http://localhost:4566` and fake credentials. Never point them at real AWS.
55	- Inside the compose network LocalStack is `http://localstack:4566`, so compose overrides the endpoint and the queue URL from each `local-test` file through environment variables. Spring drops the dash in `device-logs` when it maps a property to an environment variable: `DEVICELOGS_AWS_ENDPOINTOVERRIDE`, never `DEVICE_LOGS_...`, which is silently ignored.
56	- Keep `-XX:-UseContainerSupport` in `CLOUD8_SERVICE_PARAMS` while the base image ships JDK 17.0.2. Without it both services fail at startup on Docker Desktop (JDK-8287073).
57	- Never commit `envoy/certs/`. It holds the lab CA key, and a phone that trusts the lab CA trusts any server it signs.
58	- Pin the Envoy image to an exact version, never `latest`.
59	- Keep `proxy_100_continue: true` and the `/logs/` route's `timeout: 0s`. Without the first, Envoy sends 100 Continue itself and the phone sends the body before any check runs (ADR 0009). Envoy's default route timeout of 15 s, counted from the end of the body, would cut off an S3 write that takes up to 60 s (ADR 0005).
60	- Envoy removes every client-sent `X-Amzn-Mtls-Clientcert*` header before it adds its own, so each reaches upload-service once. A header added to `request_headers_to_add` also goes in `request_headers_to_remove`.
61	- Through Colima, Envoy sees a Docker gateway address (such as `172.19.0.1`), not the phone's IP. That address is what `source-ip` and the row's `source_ip` show locally.
62	- Envoy writes the Serial-Number header in lowercase hex. The ALB writes uppercase. upload-service only checks that the header is there and takes the serial from the leaf.
63	- The Poly root in `poly-ca-bundle.pem` comes from pki.polycom.com, SHA-256 `5A:9A:1F:57:09:02:08:B9:AC:DA:4F:23:95:10:15:39:77:AE:A2:10:89:79:15:01:4D:43:1E:FF:06:60:1E:BE`. After changing the bundle, check that a phone's chain still passes `openssl verify -CAfile local/envoy/poly-ca-bundle.pem`.
64	
65	## ADRs that bind this module
66	
67	- ADR 0004: Envoy strips client-sent `X-Amzn-Mtls-*` headers before adding its own.
68	- ADR 0005: the `/logs/` route keeps `timeout: 0s`.
69	- ADR 0009: `proxy_100_continue: true` stays on, so Envoy never answers 100 Continue itself.
70	- ADR 0011: before bumping the LocalStack pin, check a second `put-object --if-none-match '*'` fails.
71	- ADR 0017: S3 notifies the queue directly, on `raw/` only, no EventBridge.
72	- ADR 0021 and ADR 0022: the table's keys and the `customer-index` GSI match the processor's names.
73	- ADR 0023: redrive after 5 receives and the 60 s visibility timeout are queue settings in `init-aws.sh`.
74	
75	## When ...
76	
77	- When adding a resource: create it in `init-aws.sh` with an "already exists" guard, and decide whether `reset.sh` must empty it.
78	- When a change contradicts an ADR: stop and ask; don't work around it.
79

# local/CLAUDE.md

Rules for agents working in `local`. The root CLAUDE.md still applies.

## What this folder is

The local run environment: one LocalStack container (S3, SQS, DynamoDB), both services with the `local-test` profile and Envoy as the ALB stand-in for a real phone, started by `docker compose`, plus an init script that creates what the services expect. Local runs only, never deployed.

## Commands

From the repo root:

- Build the jars first, because the images copy them from `target/`: `mvn clean verify` (or `mvn package -DskipTests`). Old jars there give old behavior with no warning.
- Once, before the first start: `local/envoy/gen-certs.sh` writes the lab CA and Envoy's server certificate for this Mac's LAN IP to `local/envoy/certs/`. It takes the IP of en0; pass another as its argument. When the IP changes, run it again (it keeps the CA), then `docker compose -f local/docker-compose.yml restart envoy`. Envoy reads `envoy.yaml`, `master.cfg` and the certificates only at start, so it needs the same restart after any change to them.
- Start everything: `docker compose -f local/docker-compose.yml up -d --build`. The first build pulls the 8x8 base image and needs the VPN; later runs don't. The services start once LocalStack's healthcheck sees `init-aws.sh` finish.
- Check it: `curl -s localhost:1297/actuator/health` (upload-service) and `curl -s localhost:1299/actuator/health` (processor), both `{"status":"UP",...}`
- Check the whole path: `local/smoke-test.sh` uploads one file under a random MAC, shows the S3 object and the processor's row, and exits non-zero if a check fails
- After changing Java code: rebuild the jars, then `up -d --build` again
- Empty the bucket, the table and both queues (needs `aws` and `jq` on the host): `local/reset.sh`
- Stop and delete everything, data included: `docker compose -f local/docker-compose.yml down`
- Check that Envoy turns away anything but a Poly phone in the TLS handshake, with no HTTP response and no upload-service log line:

  ```
  IP=$(ipconfig getifaddr en0)
  curl -v --cacert local/envoy/certs/lab-ca.crt -X PUT --data-binary hello https://$IP:8443/logs/48256738509b-app.log  # alert certificate required, reason(1116) in macOS curl
  openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -days 1 -subj /CN=48256738509B -keyout /tmp/k.pem -out /tmp/c.pem
  curl -v --cacert local/envoy/certs/lab-ca.crt --cert /tmp/c.pem --key /tmp/k.pem -X PUT --data-binary hello https://$IP:8443/logs/48256738509b-app.log  # alert unknown ca
  ```

- Give a phone the lab CA, once, from your own terminal. The folder holds the certificate only, never the keys: `d=$(mktemp -d) && cp local/envoy/certs/lab-ca.crt "$d" && python3 -m http.server 8080 -d "$d"`. The phone installs `http://<lan-ip>:8080/lab-ca.crt` in Platform CA 2. Stop the server afterwards.
- Watch the phone's requests: `docker compose -f local/docker-compose.yml logs -f envoy`, one line per request. A rejected handshake writes nothing.

A phone reaches the stack only through Envoy on `https://<lan-ip>:8443`, with the VPN off, because the VPN routes all of 10.0.0.0/8. A request to 1296 skips Envoy and needs the `X-Amzn-Mtls-*` and `X-Forwarded-For` headers set by hand, with a leaf certificate whose CN is the MAC in uppercase, as `smoke-test.sh` does.

## File map

- `docker-compose.yml`: the pinned LocalStack container on port 4566, upload-service on 1296/1297 and processor on 1298/1299, built from each module's `src/main/docker/Dockerfile`, and the pinned Envoy image on 8443.
- `envoy/envoy.yaml`: the mTLS listener, the ALB headers and the routes. `/logs/` goes to upload-service, a GET of `<mac>.cfg` or `000000000000.cfg` gets `envoy/master.cfg`, everything else 404.
- `envoy/poly-ca-bundle.pem`: the three Poly CAs Envoy trusts. Public, so committed.
- `envoy/master.cfg`: the master config every phone gets. Logs and call lists go to `/logs/`.
- `envoy/gen-certs.sh`: runs on the host and writes `envoy/certs/`, which git ignores.
- `init/init-aws.sh`: runs inside the container when LocalStack is ready. Creates the bucket, the queue and its DLQ, the `raw/` notification and the table. Safe to run again.
- `reset.sh`: runs on the host against `localhost:4566`.
- `smoke-test.sh`: runs on the host against LocalStack and both services, not through Envoy. Sends the ALB headers itself, because only a phone has a certificate Envoy accepts.

## Hard rules

- Never use the `latest` LocalStack tag. Since 23 March 2026 it needs an auth token. Before changing the pinned version, check that a second `put-object` with `--if-none-match '*'` on the same key fails with `PreconditionFailed` (ADR 0011).
- The names are `device-logs-local` (bucket), `device-logs-uploads` and `device-logs-uploads-dlq` (queues), `device-logs-index` (table) and `us-west-2`. When one changes, change `init-aws.sh`, `reset.sh` and the `local-test` file of every service together.
- Redrive after 5 receives and a 60 s visibility timeout are queue settings in `init-aws.sh`, never Java constants (ADR 0023).
- S3 notifies the queue directly, on `raw/` only, with no EventBridge (ADR 0017).
- The table's sort key is named `received_at_type` and its value is `<received_at>#<type>`. The `#` stays in the value only: a `#` in an attribute name would force `ExpressionAttributeNames` on every key condition and projection. The GSI is `customer-index` on `customer_id` + `received_at` (ADR 0022).
- LocalStack does not enforce IAM, so a local pass does not prove the real queue policy or roles are right.
- Scripts here use the fixed endpoint `http://localhost:4566` and fake credentials. Never point them at real AWS.
- Inside the compose network LocalStack is `http://localstack:4566`, so compose overrides the endpoint and the queue URL from each `local-test` file through environment variables. Spring drops the dash in `device-logs` when it maps a property to an environment variable: `DEVICELOGS_AWS_ENDPOINTOVERRIDE`, never `DEVICE_LOGS_...`, which is silently ignored.
- Keep `-XX:-UseContainerSupport` in `CLOUD8_SERVICE_PARAMS` while the base image ships JDK 17.0.2. Without it both services fail at startup on Docker Desktop (JDK-8287073).
- Never commit `envoy/certs/`. It holds the lab CA key, and a phone that trusts the lab CA trusts any server it signs.
- Pin the Envoy image to an exact version, never `latest`.
- Keep `proxy_100_continue: true` and the `/logs/` route's `timeout: 0s`. Without the first, Envoy sends 100 Continue itself and the phone sends the body before any check runs (ADR 0009). Envoy's default route timeout of 15 s, counted from the end of the body, would cut off an S3 write that takes up to 60 s (ADR 0005).
- Envoy removes every client-sent `X-Amzn-Mtls-Clientcert*` header before it adds its own, so each reaches upload-service once. A header added to `request_headers_to_add` also goes in `request_headers_to_remove`.
- Through Colima, Envoy sees a Docker gateway address (such as `172.19.0.1`), not the phone's IP. That address is what `source-ip` and the row's `source_ip` show locally.
- Envoy writes the Serial-Number header in lowercase hex. The ALB writes uppercase. upload-service only checks that the header is there and takes the serial from the leaf.
- The Poly root in `poly-ca-bundle.pem` comes from pki.polycom.com, SHA-256 `5A:9A:1F:57:09:02:08:B9:AC:DA:4F:23:95:10:15:39:77:AE:A2:10:89:79:15:01:4D:43:1E:FF:06:60:1E:BE`. After changing the bundle, check that a phone's chain still passes `openssl verify -CAfile local/envoy/poly-ca-bundle.pem`.

## ADRs that bind this module

- ADR 0004: Envoy strips client-sent `X-Amzn-Mtls-*` headers before adding its own.
- ADR 0005: the `/logs/` route keeps `timeout: 0s`.
- ADR 0009: `proxy_100_continue: true` stays on, so Envoy never answers 100 Continue itself.
- ADR 0011: before bumping the LocalStack pin, check a second `put-object --if-none-match '*'` fails.
- ADR 0017: S3 notifies the queue directly, on `raw/` only, no EventBridge.
- ADR 0021 and ADR 0022: the table's keys and the `customer-index` GSI match the processor's names.
- ADR 0023: redrive after 5 receives and the 60 s visibility timeout are queue settings in `init-aws.sh`.

## When ...

- When adding a resource: create it in `init-aws.sh` with an "already exists" guard, and decide whether `reset.sh` must empty it.
- When a change contradicts an ADR: stop and ask; don't work around it.

# Envoy as the ALB stand-in for a real phone. It checks the phone's chain against the Poly CAs and
# rejects anything else in the TLS handshake, adds the headers the ALB adds, streams /logs/ to
# upload-service, and serves the master config the phone fetches at boot. Local runs only.
static_resources:
  listeners:
    - name: phones
      address:
        socket_address: { address: 0.0.0.0, port_value: 8443 }
      filter_chains:
        - transport_socket:
            name: envoy.transport_sockets.tls
            typed_config:
              "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.transport_sockets.tls.v3.DownstreamTlsContext
              # A client without a certificate the Poly CAs signed never gets an HTTP response.
              require_client_certificate: true
              common_tls_context:
                tls_params:
                  tls_minimum_protocol_version: TLSv1_2
                  tls_maximum_protocol_version: TLSv1_3
                  # The ECDHE GCM suites of ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS13-1-2-2021-06 (ADR 0003). Every lab
                  # phone offers the two RSA ones, and only on TLS 1.2.
                  cipher_suites:
                    - ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256
                    - ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256
                    - ECDHE-ECDSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384
                    - ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384
                # Made by gen-certs.sh for the Mac's LAN IP, the address the phone connects to.
                tls_certificates:
                  - certificate_chain: { filename: /etc/envoy/certs/server.crt }
                    private_key: { filename: /etc/envoy/certs/server.key }

content.text:
The repo lists three ALB behaviours that are still unverified. All three are in the "Still open" note of the 2026-10-16 lab results.

1. **Chain depth.** Phones send a leaf and two intermediates, so the chain is 4 with the root. That is exactly the ALB's depth limit of 4, and nobody has seen the ALB accept it. Until then, the plan is to watch the ALB's `ClientCertExceedsDepthLimit` metric and its connection logs.
2. **Client-sent `X-Amzn-Mtls-*` headers.** Nobody knows whether the ALB overwrites these when a client sends them. ADR 0004 is safe either way.
3. **Expired device certificates.** Device certificates last 15 years, so phones made before about late 2011 may carry expired ones. How the ALB treats them is open.

**Why Envoy can't settle them:** Envoy is a hand-configured imitation of the ALB, not the ALB. Each of these questions is about AWS's own behaviour, and locally that behaviour is whatever Envoy is told to do:
- Envoy checks the chain against the Poly CA bundle with its own TLS validation. A pass there says nothing about the ALB's depth limit or how it handles expiry.
- Envoy is set up to remove client-sent `X-Amzn-Mtls-Clientcert*` headers before adding its own. So locally the stripping is something the repo chose, not something it observed. Envoy's output also differs from the ALB's in small ways: it writes the serial number in lowercase hex where the ALB uses uppercase, and through Colima it shows a Docker gateway IP instead of the phone's.
- The lab note says outright that these checks "need a real ALB, not the Envoy stand-in in `local/`."

Files used:
- `docs/research/2026-10-16-lab-results.md`
- `local/CLAUDE.md`
- `local/envoy/envoy.yaml`
- `docs/operations/observability.md`
